newsitem.title: GERMANY: German insurance group slams Bonn tax plans.
newsitem.headline: German insurance group slams Bonn tax plans.

text.p: Germany's top insurance association, the GDV, said government plans to tax returns on life insurance clashed with a growing need to supplement state pensions and would affect millions of Germans.
Bonn's tax commission on Thursday revealed a new tax on life insurance policies, which would take effect for existing policies as of the year 2002.
In a statement, the GDV said the levy would affect 80 million insurance contracts. Some 55 million policies were designed as methods of old-age financing, the association said.
The tax would make an "irreversible hole" in these individuals' old-age provision.
Under the government's plans, holders of life insurance policies can opt to have the returns taxed annually at ten percent, or have the income included in calculated overall income tax.
